issues.description: Method mismatch: Stock.findStockIngredient. The template repository declares Stock.findStockIngredient with signature findStockIngredient(String name, boolean caseSensitive) (template/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Stock.java lines 22-30), but other methods in the same template (Stock.add and Stock.take) call findStockIngredient(String) with a single parameter (template/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Stock.java lines 32-41 and 43-57). The problem statement UML and the solution repository define/findStockIngredient as a single-parameter method findStockIngredient(String): StockIngredient (problem_statement.md lines 49-55; solution/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Stock.java lines 22-30). This mismatch causes a compilation error in the template and prevents students from building and running the project or implementing SealSaloon correctly.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template Stock.findStockIngredient signature match the problem statement and the solution: provide a single-parameter method public StockIngredient findStockIngredient(String name). Two acceptable fixes: (a) Add an overload public StockIngredient findStockIngredient(String name) that delegates to the existing two-parameter method with a chosen default (e.g., return findStockIngredient(name, false) or findStockIngredient(name, true)), or (b) change the existing method signature to public StockIngredient findStockIngredient(String name) and update its implementation accordingly. This will align the template with the UML and solution and resolve the compilation error while keeping the intended behavior.

issues.description: Concept: a lookup method that returns a StockIngredient by its name. Problem statement (UML) and the solution implementation expect a method with the signature findStockIngredient(String) returning StockIngredient. The template implementation instead declares findStockIngredient(String name, boolean caseSensitive). Because the template also calls findStockIngredient(...) with a single String argument in add() and take(), this creates a mismatch that will confuse students and causes compilation errors. Students reading the exercise will search for and try to implement/find findStockIngredient(String) but the template exposes a different API (extra boolean parameter), preventing a clear mapping between requirement and code.
